summary: pid_separation_power.py applied the heavy-particle Bethe formula to electrons and positrons, reporting a dE/dx separation as valid, and used I = 75 eV for water instead of 79.7 eV.

database_specific.introduced_basis: the defective code is in the script as first released (hep-research 0.3.0, commit 351029c0)
database_specific.outputs: skills/hep-detector/scripts/pid_separation_power.py prints JSON on stdout (mode dedx: species_a and species_b, observable, n_sigma, validity) and writes no artifact

observables: dE/dx separation and its validity (pid_separation_power.py --mode dedx)
impact.bias: e vs pi at 0.2 GeV/c gave n_sigma 3.39 with validity 'inside' (now outside the formula, no n_sigma); a muon at 0.3 GeV/c in water lost 2.05062 MeV cm^2/g instead of 2.03897
impact.trigger: an electron or positron (mass below 10 MeV) in --mode dedx, or the material water

remedy: rerun pid_separation_power.py with a release that has the fix; an electron dE/dx separation from the old output is not valid
